notes.description: Points to cover, sources, tone, length.

topic.description: What the piece is about, in one line.

body.description: The callout's Markdown, without the > quoting.

kind.description: note, tip, warning, quote … as written, e.g. NOTE.

title.description: The callout's title; empty uses its kind.

language.description: Fence language, e.g. python, bash, yaml.

document.description: The file in the document library, when it is there.

href.description: Where the site serves the file, e.g. /assets/files/report.pdf, or its full URL.

embed.description: The address of a video, post or other page to embed, e.g. a YouTube URL.

text.description: The heading text, plain, without leading #.

alt.description: Alternative text; empty only if decorative.

image.description: The id of an image in the image library.

alt.description: Accessible description of the intended plate.

image.description: The drawn plate, once it exists.

letter.description: One capital letter, A to Z.

subject.description: A concrete, drawable scene with no text in it, for the art model.

tagline.description: The line a grown-up reads aloud.

word.description: The word the letter stands for.

liquid.description: A Liquid template — an include, a loop, a capture — verbatim: the site's build evaluates it.

markdown.description: A chunk of Markdown kept verbatim: paragraphs, lists, tables, Liquid tags, includes, raw HTML and [[wikilinks]] are all allowed and are never rewritten.

page.description: The id of the page to link to.

text.description: Link text; defaults to the page title.

paragraph.description:
Rich text as Wagtail's HTML subset:

, , , ,

    ,
      ,
    • , .

raw_html.description: An HTML block, verbatim: the site's build renders it.

table.description: A Markdown pipe table: `data` is its rows of cells, the first row its header.

typed_table.description: A table whose columns each hold text or numbers; written as a Markdown pipe table.

rows.description: One value per column, in column order.

description: Block JSON an agent proposes must match this schema and is then validated by the blocks themselves. A body is a list of {type, value} blocks; `id` is assigned by the CMS.
